topItems.fixSuggestion: Render the value as text (default React escaping) or run it through DOMPurify.sanitize() first.

topItems.title: Path Traversal Risk
topItems.description: fs.writeFile() path was built from a variable. Verify it can't escape the intended directory.
topItems.fixSuggestion: Resolve to an absolute path, then verify the result starts with the expected base directory. Allowlist file ids → server-resolved paths, never echo user paths back.

findings.title: OWASP Top 10 analyzer coverage: 80% (8/10)
findings.description: TestForge ships rules for 8 of the 10 OWASP 2021 categories. Categories without dedicated rules yet: A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures, A10:2021 — Server-Side Request Forgery. These are gaps in the analyzer itself — your project may still have issues in these areas that this report won't surface.
findings.fixSuggestion: For the un-covered categories, complement TestForge with: dependency-track for A08 (software integrity), an SSRF-focused fuzzer or proxy-based runtime scan for A10. Track the gap in your threat model.

findings.fixSuggestion: Run `npm install` (or your package manager's equivalent) before the analysis, or supply pre-installed dependencies. Without this, 252 declared deps are unchecked for license compatibility.

findings.title: Estimated mutation score: ~37% (heuristic)
findings.description: Inputs: 426 test files / 6393 source files (ratio 0.07), 8625 assertions (6122 strong, 742 weak, 156 snapshot), 18 distinct strong-matcher type(s). ~12952/35007 candidate mutants likely killed. Run Stryker for the exact number.
findings.fixSuggestion: Boost the kill rate: replace `toBeTruthy()` with `toBe(specificValue)`, add boundary-condition tests, vary the matcher types you use.

findings.title: 8 test file(s) dominated by weak assertions
findings.description: Files where >50% of assertions are toBeTruthy / toBeFalsy / toBeDefined / toBeNull. Examples: apps/studio/lib/navigation.test.ts (20/32 weak); apps/studio/lib/error-reporting.test.ts (10/18 weak); apps/studio/components/layouts/OrganizationLayout.test.tsx (16/28 weak).
findings.fixSuggestion: A mutation that changes `42` to `41` still satisfies `toBeTruthy()`. Replace with `toBe(42)` or `toEqual({…})` to actually catch behaviour changes.

findings.title: 6 test file(s) dominated by snapshot assertions
findings.description: Files where ≥90% of assertions are toMatchSnapshot / toMatchInlineSnapshot. Examples: packages/pg-meta/test/views.test.ts (4/4); packages/pg-meta/test/table-privileges.test.ts (5/5); packages/pg-meta/test/schemas.test.ts (7/7).
findings.fixSuggestion: Snapshots catch SOME mutants but are brittle (changes in unrelated fields cause failures). Mix in concrete assertions on the values that actually matter.

findings.title: Mutation testing tool not configured
findings.description: Stryker Mutator or similar not found in devDependencies. Install to get real mutation scores.
findings.fixSuggestion: npm install -D @stryker-mutator/core && npx stryker init

findings.title: No property-based testing framework detected
findings.description: No `fast-check` / `jsverify` / `@fast-check/vitest` import found. Property-based testing generates inputs over a domain and asserts invariants — strong fit for parsers, encoders, math, and stateful reducers.
findings.fixSuggestion: Install `fast-check` and write a few `fc.assert(fc.property(fc.integer(), n => sortRoundTrip([n]) === [n]))`-style tests against your most invariant-heavy code.

findings.title: Potential N+1 Query in for-of
findings.description:
`query()` is invoked inside a `for-of` loop at e2e/studio/features/database.spec.ts:1111. Each iteration issues its own DB round-trip.
Line: await query(`drop type if exists ${typeName};`)
findings.fixSuggestion: Batch the query: pre-build the id list, fire one query with `WHERE id IN (...)`, or use eager-loading (`.include()` / `.populate()` / `JOIN`). For parallelisation only, wrap in `Promise.all([...].map(...))` so the round-trips overlap.

findings.title: 29 Unused Dependencies
findings.description: Dependencies not imported anywhere: @octokit/graphql, @octokit/rest, gsap, typescript, @supabase/supa-mdx-lint, …. These increase bundle size, install time, and supply-chain attack surface.
findings.fixSuggestion: Remove with: `npm uninstall @octokit/graphql @octokit/rest gsap`. Confirm with `npx depcheck` before removing — some packages are loaded by side-effect (Babel plugins, polyfills) without explicit imports.

Exports that no other file imports:

  packages/common/telemetry.tsx: handlePageLeaveTelemetry, sendTelemetryIdentify, useTelemetryIdentify, handleResetTelemetry

findings.title: Auth Endpoints Not Rate Limited
findings.description: AI agents frequently re-authenticate (token refresh, retry on 401). Without auth rate limiting, agents can brute-force or DoS your auth system.
findings.fixSuggestion: Rate limit auth endpoints separately: 5 attempts/min per IP. Add account locking after 10 failures. Monitor for unusual auth patterns.

findings.title: Heavy inline styles in 292 file(s) without CSS Modules
findings.description: 579 inline `style={{…}}` JSX props across 292 files; no CSS Modules detected. Example file: packages/dev-tools/DevToolbarTrigger.tsx.
findings.fixSuggestion: Adopt CSS Modules / Tailwind / styled-components / vanilla-extract. Inline styles defeat selector caching and make visual-diff testing unstable.

findings.title: 123 hardcoded pixel value(s) in inline styles
findings.description: Pixel values inside JSX `style={{…}}` props. These don't scale to user font-size preferences and break visual-regression snapshots across viewports.
findings.fixSuggestion: Use rem/em or design tokens. Pull from a shared theme so the snapshot baseline can move atomically.

findings.title: 49 inline color literal(s) in JSX styles
findings.description: Hex colors (#abc / #abcdef) embedded directly in `style={{…}}` props. Visual themes can't roll out (dark mode, brand changes) without grepping every file.
findings.fixSuggestion: Pull colors from a theme object (`theme.colors.primary`) or CSS variables.

findings.title: TypeScript without strict mode
findings.description: tsconfig.json found but `compilerOptions.strict` is not true. The default loose mode lets `any`-typed values flow freely; null/undefined errors slip past the compiler.
findings.fixSuggestion: Set `"strict": true` in tsconfig (turns on strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, strictFunctionTypes, etc.). For an existing codebase, use `tsc --noEmit` to see what breaks, then file by file.

findings.title: No caching layer for growing app
findings.description: 252 direct deps, no Redis / ioredis / memcached / LRU-cache. Even an in-process LRU pays off for hot paths.
findings.fixSuggestion: Cache layer for queries + sessions + rate-limit counters. Redis for cross-instance share, LRU-cache for in-process hot data.

findings.title: No observability dependency detected
findings.description: No Sentry / Datadog / NewRelic / OpenTelemetry / Honeycomb / Rollbar / Bugsnag dep. MTTR depends on knowing something broke before customers report it.
findings.fixSuggestion: Add error-tracking (Sentry is the easiest) and ideally a tracing stack (OpenTelemetry → Honeycomb / Datadog / Jaeger). Wire up alerts to a notification channel that humans actually read.

findings.title: No feature-flag platform detected
findings.description: A test framework is in place, but no LaunchDarkly / Statsig / Unleash / Flagsmith / Growthbook / Posthog SDK was found. Feature flags decouple deploy from release, enabling kill-switches and staged rollouts — proven CFR reducer.
findings.fixSuggestion: For early-stage projects: Posthog has a free tier and is JS-SDK-only. For larger teams: LaunchDarkly / Statsig. Even a homegrown flags table beats no kill-switch.
